What Happened to the Cast of Next of Kin (1989)

From Patrick Swayze's enduring legacy to Liam Neeson's action star transformation, explore how the talented cast of Next of Kin (1989) shaped Hollywood in the decades following this gritty drama. Learn about their triumphs, transitions, and the lasting impact they've left on cinema.

22 January 2025 · RewindZone Archive

The 1989 action film Next of Kin brought together an ensemble cast that would go on to shape Hollywood in the decades that followed. From future Oscar nominees to beloved character actors, the careers of these performers took fascinating turns after their collaboration in this gritty drama. Some reached the heights of Hollywood success, while others left lasting legacies before their untimely departures.

The Leading Man's Legacy: Patrick Swayze

When Next of Kin was filmed, Patrick Swayze was already a household name thanks to Dirty Dancing. At age 37 during filming, Swayze would go on to deliver one of his most memorable performances in Ghost (1990). He continued working steadily through the 1990s and 2000s, appearing in diverse roles from drag queen Vida Boheme in To Wong Foo, Thanks for Everything! Julie Newmar to motivational speaker Jim Cunningham in Donnie Darko. Despite being diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in 2008, Swayze demonstrated remarkable resilience by continuing to work on the television series The Beast. He passed away in 2009, leaving behind a rich legacy of memorable performances.

From Supporting Role to Action Star: Liam Neeson

Advertisement

At 37 during Next of Kin, Liam Neeson was still building his Hollywood career. His breakthrough came four years later with his Oscar-nominated performance in Schindler's List. However, it was his role in Taken (2008) that unexpectedly transformed him into one of Hollywood's most reliable action stars. Now 72, Neeson continues to work prolifically, recently appearing in Absolution (2024), proving his enduring appeal as both a dramatic actor and action hero.

Helen Hunt's Path to Oscar Glory

Helen Hunt was just 26 when she appeared in Next of Kin. Her career would soar in the following decades, first with her Emmy-winning role in the sitcom Mad About You and then with an Academy Award win for As Good as It Gets (1997). Hunt successfully transitioned into directing, making her directorial debut with Then She Found Me (2007). At 61, she remains active both in front of and behind the camera, directing episodes of prestigious television series and appearing in films like The Night Clerk.

Bill Paxton: A Versatile Career Cut Short

Bill Paxton went on to become one of Hollywood's most reliable character actors after Next of Kin. He delivered memorable performances in blockbusters like Aliens, Titanic, and Edge of Tomorrow, while also starring in the groundbreaking HBO series Big Love. Tragically, Paxton passed away in 2017 at age 61 due to complications from heart surgery, leaving behind a diverse body of work.

Notable Supporting Cast Members

Adam Baldwin

Advertisement

Adam Baldwin, who was 27 during filming, went on to cult fame as Jayne Cobb in Firefly and developed a successful voice-acting career.

Ted Levine

Ted Levine would later gain recognition as Buffalo Bill in The Silence of the Lambs and continued steady work in films like Heat and Shutter Island.

Ben Stiller

A young Ben Stiller also appeared in one of his earliest film roles, years before becoming a comedy superstar. At just 24 years old during filming, this minor role preceded his creation of The Ben Stiller Show for MTV and his eventual rise to fame with films like There's Something About Mary and Meet the Parents. Today, Stiller has evolved into a successful actor-director, far from his humble beginnings in supporting roles.

Andreas Katsulas

Andreas Katsulas became beloved by science fiction fans as Ambassador G'Kar in Babylon 5 before his passing in 2006.

Michael J. Pollard

Michael J. Pollard, an Oscar nominee for Bonnie and Clyde, continued character work until his death in 2019.

Del Close

Del Close, already a legendary improvisational theatre teacher during filming, influenced countless comedians before his passing in 1999.
